newsitem.title: FRANCE: Israeli embassy denies Shamir taken ill in Paris.
newsitem.headline: Israeli embassy denies Shamir taken ill in Paris.

text.p: The Israeli embassy in Paris denied on Saturday that former Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Shamir had been taken ill during a visit to the French capital, saying he was fine and sticking to his schedule.

Aides had said that Shamir, who turns 81 on October 15, was giving an interview to a French television station at his hotel when he suffered a drop in blood pressure on Friday. He cancelled a news conference and was reportedly examined by a doctor.
An embassy spokeswoman said, however, that staff had met Shamir and he was "indignant" at the report.

"He was not taken ill, he just didn't want to give the news conference," the spokeswoman said. "He is not sick, he is very well, and he is going to respect all the appointments he has planned with the Israeli community in France," she added.
"We saw Mr Shamir this morning. He was indignant, he told us the report was untrue," she said.

Shamir, a former Jewish underground fighter and spymaster who was a hardline prime minister from 1986 to 1992, is on a European fundraising tour for the Jewish National Fund (Keren Kayemet). He plans to leave Paris on Wednesday.
